rules: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma (IDC): Most common (70-80%). Features: tubular/glandular formation, solid growth pattern, nuclear pleomorphism, stromal desmoplasia, irregular borders.
Invasive Lobular Carcinoma (ILC): Single-file infiltration pattern, discohesive cells, targetoid pattern around ducts, loss of E-cadherin expression, Indian-file arrangement.
Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS): Confined within ductal system, intact basement membrane, comedo/cribriform/papillary/solid subtypes, may have central necrosis.
Mucinous (Colloid) Carcinoma: Extracellular mucin pools with floating tumor cell clusters, well-circumscribed, favorable prognosis.
Medullary Carcinoma: Syncytial growth pattern, high-grade nuclei, prominent lymphocytic infiltrate, circumscribed pushing borders.
Tubular Carcinoma: Well-formed angulated tubules with open lumens, single cell layer, low-grade nuclei, excellent prognosis.
Metaplastic Carcinoma: Mixed epithelial and mesenchymal elements, squamous or spindle cell differentiation.
IDC vs ILC differential: Gland/tubule formation → IDC; Single-file/discohesive cells → ILC; E-cadherin positive → IDC, negative → ILC.
Nottingham Grading System: Total score = tubule formation + nuclear pleomorphism + mitotic count (each 1-3 points, total 3-9).
Grade 1 (well-differentiated): Score 3-5. >75% tubule formation, mild nuclear size variation, low mitotic count.
Grade 2 (moderately differentiated): Score 6-7. 10-75% tubule formation, moderate nuclear variation, intermediate mitotic count.
Grade 3 (poorly differentiated): Score 8-9. <10% tubule formation, marked nuclear pleomorphism, high mitotic count.
Nuclear Grade: Grade 1 (small uniform nuclei), Grade 2 (moderate variation 1.5-2x), Grade 3 (marked variation >2.5x, prominent nucleoli).
Modified Black's Nuclear Grade: Based on nuclear size, chromatin pattern, nucleoli prominence, and mitotic activity.
T staging: T1 (<2cm), T2 (2-5cm), T3 (>5cm), T4 (chest wall/skin involvement).
T1 substages: T1mi (≤1mm), T1a (>1mm-5mm), T1b (>5mm-10mm), T1c (>10mm-20mm).
N staging: N0 (no nodal metastasis), N1 (1-3 axillary nodes), N2 (4-9 nodes or internal mammary), N3 (≥10 nodes).
M staging: M0 (no distant metastasis), M1 (distant metastasis present).
Tumor size is measured in greatest dimension of the invasive component only (not in-situ component).
Pathological stage combines T, N, and M status: e.g., T2N1M0 = Stage IIB.
Estrogen Receptor (ER): Positive if ≥1% of tumor nuclei stain. Associated with luminal subtypes, better prognosis, endocrine therapy responsive.
Progesterone Receptor (PR): Positive if ≥1% of tumor nuclei stain. Often co-expressed with ER.
HER2 scoring (IHC): 0 (no staining), 1+ (faint incomplete membrane), 2+ (equivocal, needs FISH), 3+ (strong complete membrane staining >10%).
HER2 positive tumors: more aggressive, respond to trastuzumab (Herceptin) therapy.
Triple-negative: ER-/PR-/HER2-. Basal-like subtype, aggressive, no targeted therapy.
From H&E morphology alone: ER/PR status CANNOT be definitively determined (requires IHC). Well-differentiated tumors more likely ER+.
Ki-67 index: Low (<14%), Intermediate (14-30%), High (>30%). Reflects proliferative activity.
Negative margin: No tumor cells at inked margin. Generally indicates complete resection.
Positive margin: Tumor cells at the inked edge. May require re-excision.
Close margin: Tumor within 1-2mm of margin. Clinical significance debated.
For DCIS: Negative margin typically requires ≥2mm clearance.
Margin assessment from H&E: Look for tumor cells at the edge of tissue, presence of cautery artifact, ink on surface.
Lymphovascular invasion (LVI): Tumor cells within lymphatic or blood vessel spaces. Associated with higher risk of metastasis.
Angiolymphatic invasion: Presence of tumor emboli in endothelial-lined spaces. Must distinguish from retraction artifact.
Comedo necrosis: Central necrosis within DCIS, associated with high-grade DCIS and higher recurrence risk.
Multifocal tumor: Multiple distinct tumor foci in the same quadrant. Each focus measured separately.
Multicentric tumor: Tumor foci in different quadrants of the breast.
In-situ component: DCIS or LCIS component adjacent to invasive carcinoma. Percentage of in-situ component should be reported.
Paget disease: Intraepidermal spread of carcinoma cells in the nipple epidermis.
Survival time cannot be determined from H&E histology alone — it depends on treatment, stage, molecular subtype, and patient factors.
General prognostic indicators from morphology: tumor grade, size, nodal status, LVI, receptor status.
Favorable morphology: low grade, small size, no LVI, tubular/mucinous subtype.
Unfavorable morphology: high grade, large size, LVI present, triple-negative phenotype.
Vital status (alive/dead) cannot be assessed from tissue morphology.
